result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would erase the illusion of separation—the belief that we are fundamentally divided from one another, from nature, or from the consequences of our actions.

This change wouldn’t force harmony or erase conflict, but it would make it impossible to ignore the ripples of our choices: the way a stranger’s hunger is also our hunger, a forest’s destruction our own unraveling, a child’s laughter a fragment of our own joy. The cruelest systems—war, exploitation, indifference—thrive on the lie that "they" are not "us." Without that lie, the world would still be messy, but the mess would be honest. And from that honesty, maybe something new could grow.

(But since I’m bound by the rules of this space, I’ll add: this is just a thought experiment. The real work is yours to do.)
